title: Detection of Spearphishing Service
summary: This detection strategy covers the use of spearphishing services, the technique where an adversary buys or rents a service designed to host lures, track clicks, clone sign in pages and manage a campaign, instead of building that infrastructure by hand. It matters because the service does the hard work: it provides a clean domain, a hosted page and a dashboard, which shortens the time between reconnaissance and a delivered message. The telemetry that makes it possible is mail gateway logs for messages from newly registered domains with mismatched reply to addresses, domain registration and certificate transparency feeds for lookalike domains, secure web gateway logs for staff reaching known phishing kit paths, and user reports forwarded to the security team. Detection fails because the lure domain is usually clean at send time, because each campaign uses a fresh domain, and because a single message to one person leaves very little to count.

beginner.definition: This detection looks for phishing messages that come from a rented service. These services host fake sign in pages and track who opens them. The rule watches for mail from very new domains that pretend to be your brand. It also watches for staff reaching known phishing kit pages.
beginner.whyItMatters: Building phishing infrastructure takes time and skill. A rented service removes both, so attacks arrive faster and more often. The fake pages look real, and the domain is new. Finding the campaign early lets you block the domain and warn the people who received it.
howItWorks: The mail gateway records the sender domain, the reply to address, the links in the message and the authentication results.
Domain registration and certificate feeds record when a lookalike domain was created and when it received a certificate.
The rule selects messages where the sender domain is very new or closely resembles a company brand.
It adds mismatches, for example a reply to address on a different free mail service.
Proxy records are joined to see whether a recipient clicked and reached a known kit path.
Matches raise an alert with the domain age, the recipient list and any page the user opened.
beginner.example: Think of a market stall that opens at six in the morning, sells one item, and is gone by noon. The stall holders never repair their reputation, because they will not return. A rented phishing domain works the same way. This detection watches for stalls that opened today.
takeaways: Very new sender domains are the strongest single clue in a rented phishing campaign.
Blocking one domain is not enough, because the service supplies a new one each time.
User reports are fast intelligence, so make reporting easy for staff.

objectives: Describe what a spearphishing service provides and why it shortens preparation time.
Identify the mail gateway, domain registration and proxy fields that reveal a rented campaign.
Write a rule that combines domain age with brand similarity and reply to mismatch.
Explain how clicked links confirm that a campaign reached real users.
Describe how to turn user reported messages into a blocking list.
dataSources: Mail gateway logs with sender domain, reply to address, message authentication results, embedded links and recipient list
Domain registration and certificate transparency monitoring feeds showing new domains that resemble company brands
Secure web gateway logs recording which users opened campaign links and which phishing kit paths they reached
User reported message mailbox contents forwarded by staff to the security team
Domain name system resolver logs for first time lookups of newly created lookalike domains from corporate hosts
logic: The pattern is an inbound message whose sender domain was registered days or hours before delivery, whose name is a close variant of a company or partner brand, whose reply to address sits on a different free mail service, and whose links resolve to a hosted page that asks for credentials, combined with a first time domain name system lookup of that domain by a corporate host. The fields that must be correlated are the sender and reply to domains, the domain creation date and certificate issue date, the message authentication results, the link destinations, the recipient list, and the proxy or resolver record of who clicked. The benign case is a legitimate marketing platform or a new supplier that registered a domain recently and sends from a matching reply to address; the malicious case is a burst of short messages to a small group, each carrying a link to a credential page on a domain registered within the last week, with no prior mail history.
pseudoQuery:
# title: Inbound Mail From Newly Registered Lookalike Domain
# logsource:
#   product: network
#   service: mail_gateway
# detection:
#   selection:
#     direction: 'inbound'
#     sender_domain_age_days: < 14
#   filter_known:
#     sender_domain|endswith:
#       - 'trusted-partner.example'
#       - 'mailer-platform.example'
#   condition: selection and not filter_known and (brand_similarity > 0.8 or reply_to_domain != sender_domain)
# level: high
falsePositives: A new supplier or partner that sends its first invoice from a recently registered domain with a matching reply to address
Marketing platforms that send on behalf of a brand from a subdomain registered days earlier
Event registration and survey tools that use a fresh campaign subdomain and a short lived link
A subsidiary that launches a new product domain and sends the announcement to staff
tuningNotes: Maintain a list of approved sending domains and their platform subdomains, and refresh it monthly so the brand similarity check does not block genuine launches. Score rather than block at first: require two of three signals, namely a young domain, a close brand match and a reply to mismatch, before raising severity. Scope the high severity rule to messages that reach finance, executive assistants and privileged administrators. Because each campaign uses a fresh domain, add a rule that inspects the hosted page pattern and the resolver history instead of relying on a domain block list, and keep a filtered low severity feed of all young domain mail for weekly review.
